name: Your Healthcare Operations Platform: Intake and Document Triage First

parameters.content:
## Your Healthcare Operations Platform: Intake and Document Triage First

### How it works
- Staff send an intake item or document from the portal; role checked, patient identifiers masked.
- Matched only against the active version of your policies, SOPs, forms and service guidelines.
- Claude triages and cites its sources; OpenAI is the fallback; nothing clinical is decided by the AI.
- Confident, cited items become a task in your internal tools; the rest go to the review queue.
- Every action gets its own audit row; editing a document re-indexes it, KB 1 to KB 4.

### Setup
- This canvas is the working prototype of workflow one, the thing I would build first.
- Production: a Python FastAPI service on Supabase Postgres with pgvector, Auth and row-level permissions; LangGraph only once a workflow needs loops.
- The staff web app and admin screen read the same tables: intake items, review queue, audit log.
- New workflows reuse the same retrieval, review queue and audit log, so nothing gets rebuilt.

### What I need from you
- Your staff queues and which roles may submit intake
- API access to your internal tools or CRM-style system
- A first set of policies, SOPs, forms and service guidelines
- Before any real patient data: a signed BAA with each model and hosting provider

nodes.name: Overview

parameters.content:
## 1 - INTAKE SUPPORT AND DOCUMENT TRIAGE

Your part 1, intake support and document triage; its internal task routing lands in section 4. Staff send an item from the portal, their role is checked and patient identifiers are masked before any model sees it.

nodes.name: Section - 1 - INTAKE SUPPORT AND DOCUMENT TRIAGE

parameters.content:
## 2 - RAG OVER YOUR POLICIES, SOPS, FORMS AND SERVICE GUIDELINES

Your part 2, and your question on keeping the AI useful as the knowledge base grows: each item is matched only against the active version of your own documents, filtered by service line and by what the staff role may see. When an admin edits a document, KB 1 to KB 4 re-index it and retire the old version, so no answer cites an outdated SOP; items with no matching passage are logged as gaps, so admins see what to write next.

nodes.name: Section - 2 - RAG OVER YOUR POLICIES, SOPS, FORMS AND SERVICE GUIDELINES

parameters.content:
## 3 - CLAUDE FIRST, OPENAI AS FALLBACK, CLEAR BOUNDARIES

Your part 3: Claude triages from the matched passages only, cites them and never makes a clinical call. If Claude fails, OpenAI runs the same rules; anything unsure, uncited or clinical goes to a person.

nodes.name: Section - 3 - CLAUDE FIRST, OPENAI AS FALLBACK, CLEAR BOUNDARIES

parameters.content:
## 4 - ROUTE THE TASK OR SEND IT TO THE REVIEW QUEUE

Your parts 4 and 5: the API call into your internal tools, and the review queue behind your admin screen. Confident, cited items become a task in the right queue; everything else waits for staff to approve, edit or reject it.

nodes.name: Section - 4 - ROUTE THE TASK OR SEND IT TO THE REVIEW QUEUE

parameters.content:
## 5 - AUDIT TRAIL, PERMISSIONS AND THE STAFF SCREEN

Your parts 6 and 7: logging, permissions and audit trail, then the staff web interface. Permissions are checked at steps 2 and 3 and filter retrieval at step 6; every action, that check included, gets its own append-only audit row with who, what, which sources and which model, and the staff screen shows status, owner, next steps and sources in plain words. Every later workflow reuses sections 2 to 5 as they are, so new workflows can be added without rebuilding the entire system.

nodes.name: Section - 5 - AUDIT TRAIL, PERMISSIONS AND THE STAFF SCREEN

parameters.content:
## 6 - IF ANY STEP FAILS

The item is held for manual handling, the failure is logged, and the admin screen is flagged with no patient details in the alert, so nothing sits silently.

parameters.query:
SELECT COALESCE(json_agg(t ORDER BY t.similarity DESC), '[]'::json) AS passages,
       COALESCE(MAX(t.similarity), 0) AS top_similarity
FROM (
  SELECT chunk_id, doc_id, doc_title, doc_type, version, section_heading, content,
         1 - (embedding <=> $1::vector) AS similarity
  FROM kb_chunks
  WHERE status = 'active'
    AND (service_line = $2 OR service_line = 'all')
    AND $3 = ANY (visible_to_roles)
  ORDER BY embedding <=> $1::vector
  LIMIT 6
) t;

nodes.name: 6 - Supabase: Find the Matching Policy, SOP and Form Passages
7 - Found a Passage That Covers This Item?
KB 1 - Admin Saves or Edits a Policy, SOP, Form or Guideline
KB 2 - Split Into Passages Tagged With Doc, Version, Section
KB 3 - OpenAI: Embed Every Passage in One Call

parameters.query:
WITH retired AS (
  UPDATE kb_chunks SET status = 'retired', retired_at = now()
  WHERE doc_id = $1 AND status = 'active'
  RETURNING chunk_id
), logged AS (
  INSERT INTO audit_log (staff_user_id, execution_id, action, outcome, detail, created_at)
  VALUES ($7, $8, 'kb_document_reindexed', 'active', $1 || ' now v' || $5, now())
)
INSERT INTO kb_chunks (chunk_id, doc_id, doc_title, doc_type, service_line, visible_to_roles, version, section_heading, content, embedding, status, created_at)
SELECT p.chunk_id, $1, $2, $3, $4, $6::text[], $5, p.section_heading, p.content, e.embedding::vector, 'active', now()
FROM jsonb_to_recordset($9::jsonb) AS p(idx int, chunk_id text, section_heading text, content text)
JOIN jsonb_to_recordset($10::jsonb) AS e("index" int, embedding text) ON e."index" = p.idx
RETURNING chunk_id, version;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ (() => { const d = $('KB 1 - Admin Saves or Edits a Policy, SOP, Form or Guideline').item.json.body; return [d.doc_id, d.doc_title, d.doc_type, d.service_line || 'all', String(d.version), '{' + (d.visible_to_roles || []).join(',') + '}', d.edited_by, $execution.id, JSON.stringify($('KB 2 - Split Into Passages Tagged With Doc, Version, Section').item.json.passages), JSON.stringify($json.data)]; })() }}

nodes.name: KB 4 - Supabase: Store the New Version, Retire the Old One

messageValues.message: You triage administrative intake items for a healthcare services business. You support office staff with paperwork; you do not replace clinical judgment. Hard boundaries: never diagnose, never assess symptoms, never suggest treatment or medication, and never judge how urgent care is. If the item describes symptoms, asks a clinical question or suggests a patient's health may be at risk, set category to clinical_question and needs_human to true, write one neutral line in summary_for_staff and stop. Use only the SOURCES passages you are given. Every next step must be supported by a passage you cite by chunk_id. If the sources do not cover the item, or two queues fit equally well, set needs_human to true and say why in reason. Never invent a policy, form name, deadline, fee, phone number or queue. Patient identifiers are masked as [NAME], [DATE], [PHONE], [EMAIL], [SSN] and [MEMBER_ID]; never guess or restore them, and do not repeat them in your summary. owner_queue must be exactly one of the ALLOWED QUEUES. priority is administrative only: time_sensitive when the document states a deadline, otherwise routine. confidence is your honest probability, 0 to 1, that category and owner_queue are right given the sources; stay below 0.8 when the document is partial, unreadable or contradicts the sources. Return only the requested fields as JSON.

parameters.query:
UPDATE intake_items
SET status = $2, owner_queue = $3, staff_summary = $4, next_steps = $5::jsonb,
    cited_sources = $6::jsonb, ai_model = $7, ai_confidence = $8, task_ref = $9, updated_at = now()
WHERE item_id = $1
RETURNING item_id, status, owner_queue, staff_summary, next_steps, cited_sources, ai_model, ai_confidence, task_ref, updated_at;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ (() => { const s = $('12 - Build One Audit Row per Action Taken').first().json.screen; return [s.item_id, s.status, s.owner_queue, s.staff_summary, JSON.stringify(s.next_steps || []), JSON.stringify(s.cited_sources || []), s.ai_model, s.ai_confidence, s.task_ref || null]; })() }}

15 - Any Step Fails, Anywhere

parameters.query:
WITH held AS (
  UPDATE intake_items SET status = 'manual_handling', updated_at = now()
  WHERE execution_id = $1
  RETURNING item_id
), logged AS (
  INSERT INTO audit_log (item_id, execution_id, action, outcome, detail, created_at)
  SELECT item_id, $1, 'workflow_failed', 'manual_handling', 'stopped at ' || $2, now() FROM held
)
INSERT INTO admin_alerts (execution_id, failed_step, message, created_at)
VALUES ($1, $2, 'Intake triage stopped at ' || $2 || '. The item is held for manual handling; details are in the n8n execution log.', now())
RETURNING id, failed_step;
